actions-list.actionItem: Pursuant to the order of yesterday, the Journal of the proceedings of the Senate was deemed approved to date.
Pursuant to the order of yesterday,the morning hour being deemed expired, and the times for the recognition of the two leaders being reserved.
The following transactions of morning business occurred on today.

H.R. 1190 (Rep. Downing):
        A bill to amend the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to expand access to capital for rural-area small businesses, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 1550 (Rep. Stefanik):
        A bill to redesignate Saratoga National HistoricalPark as Saratoga National Battlefield Park.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 1744 (Rep. Smith):
        To extend and authorize annual appropriations for the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom through December 31, 2028.

        -- Senate Committee on Foreign Relations discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 1945 (Rep. Onder):
        A bill to designate the America's National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 3620 (Rep. Begich):
        A bill to provide for the conveyance of certain property to the Southcentral Foundation located in Anchorage, Alaska, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 5284 (Rep. Smucker):
        A bill to require the Social Security Administration to make changes to the social security terminology used in the rules, regulation, guidance, or other materials of the Administration.

        -- Senate Committee on Finance discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 9340 (Rep. Evans):
        A bill to amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to establish a Federal standard relating to the recovery of the full, incremental costs of upgrades that serve large-load customers, and for other purposes.

        -- Motion to proceed to consideration of measure made in Senate.


 H.R. 10159 (Rep. Hudson):
        A bill to authorize the Secretary of the Army to convey to the State of North Carolina a certain parcel of real property located at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on which the State shall construct aveterans' State home, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on Armed Services discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 528 (Sen. Peters):
        A bill to reauthorize the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 6843 (Sen. Peters):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 6843 proposed by Senator Thune for Senator Peters.

        --Amendment SA 6843 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 1574 (Sen. Cortez Masto):
        A bill to amend the Stored Communications Act to include Tribal courts as courts of competent jurisdiction.

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 6844 (Sen. Cortez Masto):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 6844 proposed by Senator Thune for Senator Cortez Masto.

        --Amendment SA 6844 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S. 3219 (Sen. Heinrich):
        A bill to transfer certain Federal land into trustfor certain Indian Pueblos in the State of New Mexico, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 3383 (Sen. Schatz):
        A bill to amend the Act of August 9, 1955, to makeimprovements to that Act, and for other purposes.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 5045 (Sen. Curtis):
        A bill to amend the Clean Air Act to modify the handling of air quality monitoring with respect to prescribed fires, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 5600 (Sen. Armstrong):
        A bill to reauthorize the Traumatic Brain Injury program.

        -- Introduced in the Senate, read twice, considered, read the third time, and passed without amendment by Voice Vote.


 S.J.Res. 197 (Sen. Baldwin):
        A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services of the Departmentof Health and Human Services relating to "Patient Protection and AffordableCare Act, HHS Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters for 2027; and Basic Health Program".

        -- Motion to proceed to consideration of measure rejected in Senate by Yea-NayVote. 48 - 51. Record Vote Number: 251 



 S.Res. 662 (Sen. Kelly):
        A resolution honoring the life and service of United States Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets, expressing condolences to his family, and condemning cartel violence.

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 917 (Sen. Banks):
        A resolution expressing support for the designation of September as "Dystonia Awareness Month" to promote public awareness and understanding of dystonia.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 922 (Sen. Hoeven):
        A resolution designating October 26, 2026, as the "Day of the Deployed."

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 923 (Sen. Boozman):
        A resolution expressing support for the designation of October 4 through October 10, 2026, as "National 4-H Week".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 924 (Sen. Shaheen):
        A resolution designating October 7, 2026, as "Energy Efficiency Day" in celebration of the economic and environmental benefits that have been driven by private sector innovation and Federal energy efficiency policies.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 925 (Sen. Moody):
        A resolution designating September 2026 as "National Spinal Cord Injury Awareness Month"

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 926 (Sen. Reed):
        A resolution designating September 2026 as "National Literacy Month".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 927 (Sen. Grassley):
        A resolution designating the week beginning October 18, 2026, as "National Character Counts Week".

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 928 (Sen. Thune):
        A resolution to authorize testimony, document production, and representation by the Senate Legal Counsel in the case of United States v. Terry.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.
By unanimous consent, on the request of Mr. Thune, at  8:16 p.m., the Senate adjourned, under its order of today, until 10:15 a.m. tomorrow.
